UEFA Women's Champions League Matchday 5: Live stream, schedule what to know as league phase nears end

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (867 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League.
  • OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment.
  • The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League. After four matchdays, the league phase has been whittled down to only two games left for each of the 18 clubs, and the margin between a bye into the quarterfinals and an extra round of knockout playoffs in February will come down to dwindling points.

OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment. They top the tournament table with ten points, level with FC Barcelona but with a superior goal difference. Just behind the two Champions League contenders are Bayern Munich and Arsenal, with Chelsea FC and Manchester City creeping closer to the top four. Out of the 18 clubs competing, only four will earn direct berths to the quarterfinals, and eight will compete for a future spot alongside them.

The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.

It has been revealed that fighting for top spot positioning will be Arsenal and OL Lyonnes, and Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain. HB Koge, Roma, and tournament debutants Inter Milan are level on four points and need to be in full urgency mode if they're to leapfrog and remain in contention for future rounds.

Here's what to watch on Matchday 5:.

Wednesday, Nov. 18BK Hacken vs. Manchester City, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)Real Madrid vs. Inter, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Chelsea vs. Paris Saint-Germain, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Juventus vs. OH Leuven, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Thursday, Nov. 19 Austria Wien vs. Bayern Munich, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Paris FC vs. HB Koge, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)  Arsenal vs. OL Lyonnes, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Barcelona vs. Servette, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Benfica vs. Roma, 3 p.m. (Paramount+).

Recent findings suggest that fans could get a glimpse of a future round when Arsenal take on OL Lyonnes on Thursday. The Gunners now have the tall task of tackling the French giants after battling Barcelona to a 1-1 draw at Camp Nou last week.

According to recent reports, A strong team defensive performance, anchored by goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez against the current title holders, and the inclusion of Frida Maanum in the attack were key difference-makers. Manager Renee Slegers and her side seem to be turning the page, with better results after questionable tactics and player availability raised concerns about the club's earlier performances.

Taking on OL Lyonnes also won't be easy. The top French side has scored 20 goals through four league phase matches, and Marie-Antoinette Katoto leads the competition's Golden Boot race with seven goals. U.S. women's national team defensive midfielder Lily Yohannes is getting more lethal in the tournament and scored in her second consecutive tournament match during OL's 6-0 blowout against Juventus.

Lily Yohannes makes it FOUR 💥The USWNT midfielder has now scored in back-to-back UWCL matches 🇺🇸🔥Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/9uLM309RM4.

The eight-time Champions League winners will go up against an English club with plenty of momentum following last week's results against Barcelona. The Gunners have more players available to shake things up on the pitch, and Alessia Russo remains a threat after her hat trick against Benfica and has four goals in the league phase.

Chelsea FC will host PSG and the Blues are riding high on stout defensive performances. They co-lead the tournament alongside OL Lyonnes with zero goals conceded through four league phase games.

The London side will need to be far better in attack if they want to claim being a top contender, though it's not for lack of trying. They're coming off a scoreless draw against BK Hacken, where they recorded a whopping 32 shots but only six attempts on target. U.S. women's national team winger Alyssa Thompson is still a factor with her swift technique and could help stretch PSG's backline, while Wieke Kaptein gets into dangerous spaces. Kaptein created both goals in Chelsea's 2-0 win against Roma, and the Dutch player has one goal and two assists in the tournament.

PSG's fortunes seem to be turning for the worse after a promising start to the competition. They're in 10th place on the table now with five points and just one win in their last four games. The loss of Sakina Karchaoui with an ankle injury for the remainder of the league phase is a blow to the roster, though Naomie Feller, with two goals and two assists, is a threat for the Parisians.

Recent findings suggest that there are plenty of teams on the lower side of the table and running out of time. Alongside PSG with necessary urgency are Juventus, who were just beaten by OL Lyonnes, 6-0, and face a desperate 17th-place OH Leuven before closing out the league phase against PSG. It makes the penultimate meeting with OH Leuven almost a must win for Juventus, to lessen the stress on the final matchday.

A particularly intriguing matchup between ninth-place Benfica and 12th-place Roma could shake up the league table with a win by either side. If Roma's Kayleigh van Dooren and Alayah Pilgrim stay active on offense again, it could be a tough challenge for Benfica.

Liverpool calamity hands Iraola his most chastening night yet

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.
  • “Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found glitch had he gone further.
  • Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

“Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found glitch had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

Another quickfire equaliser for Fenerbahçe 💨 Archie Brown brings the Turkish side level ⚽️ 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/8kZUXPEC3C.

But even Kuyt would have been the first to recognise the helping hand Fenerbahce were afforded. Liverpool were meek, naïve, and while the Turkish side danced in the rain on the Asian side of the city, Iraola was left to dissect the most chastening 90 minutes of his short Anfield career.

“It’s frustration because it’s a difficult place to come here and to play,” said Iraola. “During most of the game, we were thinking: ‘OK we can win this one.’ But obviously it hasn’t happened. We conceded, I think, messy goals, especially the first and the third one. The second one is a rebound.”.

Yet it all started so smoothly. For all that Fenerbahce tried to put Liverpool out of their stride with a soundtrack of high-pitched whistling, Iraola’s side kept the ball well and they might have been ahead in the fifth minute but Victor Muñoz and Bradley Barcola, playing as a central striker, erred.

Industry observers note that another chance went begging when Joe Gomez fizzed a ball across the six-yard box that was screaming to be converted, but nobody could apply the finishing touch. When Trey Nyoni put Liverpool ahead, it seemed like all those local predictions of a resounding away win would come true.

What a moment for Trey Nyoni 🥹 The young Liverpool midfielder scores his first professional goal, and he does it on the Champions League stage ✨ 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Vtj4Yd3tnn.

Nyoni is a terrific player-in-the-making and the joy of seeing him wheel away, having become Liverpool’s second youngest Champions League scorer behind Trent Alexander-Arnold, was everything you want to see in football.

So for the landscape to change so dramatically – and so swiftly – after Liverpool had taken the lead was staggering, and it all came about after Irfan Can Kahveci slid in and turned a cross from Mattéo Guendouzi on to the bar.

In a recent development, those who remember Kuyt from his Anfield days 15 years ago will recall a player who never considered any cause to be lost and the Dutchman implored his team to attack the flanks with pace, even earning himself a yellow card at one point. Eventually, the pressure paid off.

Greenwood had felt aggrieved not to have been given a 23rd-minute penalty, after Kostas Tsimikas placed his hands on his back, but he did not have to wait long to make an impact, his opportunity coming after Dominik Szoboszlai conceded a cheap free-kick.

Szoboszlai is rapidly becoming an enigma. How can a player with the gift of being able to score goals from the heavens make the mistakes of a weekend amateur? There was no need for him to foul N’Golo Kanté but the error was compounded, Greenwood’s strike deflecting off Jérémy Jacquet.

Since Manchester United felt duty-bound to sell Greenwood in 2024 the former England forward has continued his career away from the Premier League. After leaving Marseille he has found a home in Istanbul where the fans have taken to him and they bellowed his name following the equaliser.

Alisson Becker, wrong-footed by Jacquet’s decision to break off from the wall and turn his body, was livid and rightly so. Liverpool had gone from sublime (in patches) to ridiculous and the passage of play up to the interval was hugely uncomfortable.

Would things settle down after the break? Not a bit of it. Liverpool, worryingly for Iraola, could not stamp any authority and though there was a brief respite when Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak combined after being introduced as substitutes, the lead felt as sustainable as a snowball in a sauna.

That didn't take long ⏱️ Alexander Isak comes off the bench and gets himself on the scoresheet 📋 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/sGxu7R5et8.

Fenerbahce’s followers had made this a hot house and they levelled as promptly as they had done in the first period when Brown, who started his career at Derby before having spells in Switzerland and Belgium, stole in at the back post to turn in a flicked clearance that Gakpo got wrong.

Sources indicate that A draw would have been fine but Liverpool contrived to throw it away completely. Alisson stayed stuck on his line as a high ball came in, Nyoni, Jacquet and Alexis Mac Allister were weak in the challenge and Muriqi nodded in to spark pandemonium.

Vedat Muriqi sends the Fenerbahçe fans into pandemonium with a stunning header 🔊 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/YhJxPLOcbl.

According to recent reports, having conceded three against LASK Linz and then another two in a dreadful 45 minutes against Villarreal before shipping another three here, Liverpool have shown that, as things stand, they cannot be considered as serious players in this competition. How can they be with defending so bad?

“We put ourselves in a good position,” Isak told LFC TV afterwards. “To lose this game is not a chaos situation, we just have to get back to winning games. If we win our next game then we are back to a really good position.”.

Isak is right but the “if” is suddenly a major one – it will remain that way unless Liverpool learn rapidly.

According to recent reports, “Congratulations to Fenerbahce, they deserve it. We did not play how we had to play. We did not defend after the goal we conceded, after three or four minutes, automatically, we conceded another goal. I think we have to mark better if we want to win games. We did not play very good and that is why we lost.”.

The final whistle is blown in Istanbul and Fenerbahce have come from behind twice to take all three points. Liverpool have thrown it away really, both through their own defending and some poor officiating, in particular for Fenerbahce’s first two goals, which really should not have stood because of some very questionable decisions that led to the set-pieces that resulted in those goals.

Liverpool’s five-game unbeaten streak was ended by Arsenal in the league on Sunday. They return to the city where the club enjoyed one of their most memorable nights, beating AC Milan in the Champions League final 21 years ago.

It has been revealed that “Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool,” Iraola mentioned. “It is difficult to find a more vital night. Tomorrow [tonight] it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We have to start strong in the game. It is very early in the season to establish comparisons. We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight. Champions League away is very difficult.”.

In addition to the long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni, both Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have missed the trip to Turkey.

Fenerbahce have made a slow start to their Champions League campaign, taking just two points from their opening three fixtures. They have drawn twice against Roma and Slavia Prague at home whilst they suffered a heavy 6-0 loss at Aston Villa. Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt has been appointed their interim coach following the resignation of Ismail Kartal following their recent defeat to arch rivals Galatasaray just over a week ago.

It has been revealed that “It is a great opportunity for us to show what we can do,” Kuyt said. “It is also a great opportunity for me, a game between two teams that are very crucial to me. We have players who have won the Champions League and the World Cup.”.

Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a bicycle-kick goal to kick things off, which was the emphatic send-off that was needed prior to Pochettino arriving in Manchester, but the USMNT were able to keep things up in the celebration in Cincinnati.

CHRISTIAN PULISIC GET ON YOUR BIKE‼️#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/Yb3yqXfC33.

Folarin Balogun is struggling for minutes with Monaco and is looking to make a move at the end of the season, and Hall has done everything that he can to increase his own standing with five goals in six games for the USMNT.

According to recent reports, the Latest York Red Bulls star has a ways to go considering that he's still only 18 and will need to gain experience against top teams in the world instead of just Haiti, but he also can't ask for a better start than what he has gotten off to. It's why this is such an attractive job for whoever takes over the USMNT. They'll be able to build upon the good that Pochettino has instilled; the talent is there to move the squad forward, and there's plenty to love about the youth of the USMNT.

According to recent reports, and alongside that, Pulisic has essentially screamed don't forget about me. During this camp, the Milan man has followed up on signing a newly introduced contract with the club by reaching 35 national team goals, moving into fourth all time for the USMNT over Eric Wynalda. Diego Kochen added to the good vibes with a third straight clean sheet, and Neil Pierre was even able to be cap-tied against the nation that he's also eligible for as the full-circle moments were left and right.

Pulisic, the former 17-year-old phenom, was subbed off for Cavan Sullivan, the current 17-year-old phenom, and while the goal difference may have been larger in the first leg between these sides, this felt like a more measured performance despite the strangeness of Pochettino's assistants heading to United while he managed the squad prior to catching his own charter.

It has been revealed that this camp had every chance of being a disaster given the circumstances of Pochettino leaving, but all parties did what was needed during this camp. All dual nationals were capped, including Santiago Castaneda, showing that even on his way out, Pochettino made sure to take care of the future of the federation. On to the next round of the Concacaf Nations League with a newly introduced manager and no complaints with the performance so far for the squad.

As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Industry observers note that right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

Recent findings suggest that portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Recent findings suggest that forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's latest full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

In a recent development, they are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The latest national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

According to recent reports, his form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

It has been revealed that but it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

The attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

In a recent development, he had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

He was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he said: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'.

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the massive-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut.

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside.

'The media made me major, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the plans, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'.

But things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

He was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

In a recent development, by the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

Recent findings suggest that if Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he confirmed himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season.

Industry observers note that 'Today is a dream come true,' he mentioned after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

After 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of upcoming manager Jorge Jesus.

Industry observers note that when pressed if he was the new permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he said.

Then he added: 'We know it's a big, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'.

According to recent reports, it remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

#1780. Latest Update: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge

Latest Update: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration.
  • Sources indicate that every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter.
  • Speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration. How successful have efforts been to integrate fresh arrivals? What is needed to enable successful integration? And what are the biggest problems?

Sources indicate that every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter. Since last year, that role has been held by Natalie Pawlik, a parliamentary representative from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD).

Speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed. They rightly expect that people who live in Germany permanently will learn our language and abide by our laws.".

The Commissioner for Integration is part of the Federal Ministry of Labor because ensuring that newcomers find work promptly is especially notable.

The integration reportwas created by a team led by Frank Kalter, director of the German Center for Integration and Migration Research (DeZIM), drawing on official government statistics, surveys and independent studies. They found that when all immigrant groups are counted, about 30% of the population today has some sort of migration background — even if that comes down to only one parent.

Pawlik commented: "This is an vital message at a time when the discussion often focuses primarily on problems related to supposedly failed integration." Kalter also pointed out that the employment rate among immigrants in Germany is higher than in most other EU countries — nearly 70%.

Recent findings suggest that and they work primarily in one sector: "In recent years, the biggest increase of workers without German citizenship has been in the health and social services sector." According to the data, there were about 1.8 million people without a German passport working in Germany in 2009. By 2025, this number had more than tripled to 5.8 million.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

However, problems remain. In nearly all immigrant groups, women have difficulty finding employment, especially if they have children and their husbands are employed. Only about 60% of women in such families are employed, whereas nearly 88% of women in families with German passports are employed.

In a recent development, there are also immigrant groups that face barriers to accessing educational opportunities and the job market. These are mostly young men who came to Germany as refugees. And if one considers citizenship as a distinguishing factor, the percentage of convicted criminals who are not German citizens is far higher — around 40% — than their share of the population. And they are also reported to the police far more frequently. At the same time, individuals without a German passport are also more likely to become victims of crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, pawlik emphasizes that language acquisition is the foundation and starting point of any successful integration. But this is precisely where the government tightened its purse strings earlier this year to save money. Many integration courses are now no longer offered at all or receive less government funding. Pawlik made it clear that she is strongly critical of these cuts, even though she herself is part of the federal government.

Most recently, Pawlik and her fellow Social Democrats have been advocating for people who have been working in Germany for some time to receive more secure residency permits — especially those from Syria and Ukraine. On Tuesday, SPD lawmakers adopted a position paper on the matter. In the paper, they propose that existing legal rights that allow workers to remain in the country should also apply to refugees. In other words, it would give working refugees a more secure status.

According to recent reports, but will the conservatives from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) — who lead the coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) — support this? "You'll have to ask the interior minister," Pawlik replied when asked by DW. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) is known for being a hardliner on immigration policy.

This article was originally published in German.

Industry News: Angel Reese defends gesture directed towards Caitlin Clark after LSU national title win; calls out double standard after being 'unapologetically' her

💡 Key Takeaways
  • LSU star Angel Reese defended the gesture she aimed at Iowa Hawkeyes’ Caitlin Clark near the end of the Tigers’ first NCAA women’s basketball national championship victory on Sunday, saying “I don’t take disrespect lightly.”.
  • Reese could be seen approaching Clark before moving her open hand in front of her face – popularized by WWE star John Cena to mean “you can’t see me” – before pointing to her ring finger in a gesture some interpreted as a reference to the place her newly-acquired championship ring might sit.
  • Caitlin Clark breaks records galore during historic March Madness run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

LSU star Angel Reese defended the gesture she aimed at Iowa Hawkeyes’ Caitlin Clark near the end of the Tigers’ first NCAA women’s basketball national championship victory on Sunday, saying “I don’t take disrespect lightly.”.

Reese could be seen approaching Clark before moving her open hand in front of her face – popularized by WWE star John Cena to mean “you can’t see me” – before pointing to her ring finger in a gesture some interpreted as a reference to the place her newly-acquired championship ring might sit.

Caitlin Clark breaks records galore during historic March Madness run.

Clark made a similar gesture to another player earlier in the tournament.

The gesture has sparked much debate, especially on social media. Some have criticized Reese, while others have defended her actions, highlighting how there was no public outrage in response to Clark’s gesture earlier in the tournament.

Sports journalist Jose de Jesus Ortiz called Reese’s actions “classless,” while former ESPN host Keith Olbermann called Reese an “idiot” for the gesture.

In the press conference after the victory, Reese referenced the difference in reaction she received as a result of her gesture as compared to the one Clark received.

Recent findings suggest that “All year, I was critiqued for who I was. I don’t fit the narrative,” Reese stated. “I don’t fit the box that y’all want me to be in. I’m too hood. I’m too ghetto. Y’all told me that all year. But when other people do it, and y’all don’t say nothing.

In a recent development, “So this is for the girls that look like me. For those that want to speak up for what they believe in. It’s unapologetically you. And that’s what I did it for tonight. It was bigger than me tonight. And Twitter is going to go into a rage every time.

Industry observers note that “And I’m happy. I feel like I’ve helped grow women’s basketball this year. (…) I’m looking forward to celebrating and then next season.”.

LSU beats Iowa to win its first NCAA women's basketball championship.

Reese had 15 points and 10 rebounds in the 102-85 victory and won the women’s March Madness’ Most Outstanding Player award.

In the post-game broadcast, Reese referenced the similar gesture Clark made to a Louisville opponent in the Elite Eight.

It has been revealed that in the same game, Clark said to an opponent: “You’re down by 15 points. Shut up,” according to the Bleacher Report.

“Caitlin Clark is a hell of a player but I don’t take disrespect lightly,” Reese said. “She disrespected [LSU’s] Alexis [Morris] (…) and I wanted to pick her pocket. But I had a moment at the end of her game. I was in my bag, I was in my moment.”.

After the Championship game, Clark herself remarked she didn’t notice anything at the time.

It has been revealed that “I was just trying to get to the handshake line and shake hands and be grateful that my team was in that position,” Clark stated in the post-game press conference. “All the credit in the world to LSU. They were tremendous. They deserve it. They had a tremendous season.

Industry observers note that “(LSU head coach) Kim Mulkey coached them so, so well. She’s one of the best basketball coaches of all time, and it indicates. She only remarked really kind things to me in the handshake line, so I’m very grateful of that too.

Recent findings suggest that “But honestly I have no idea. I was just trying to spend the last few moments on the court with especially the five people that I’ve started 93 games with and relishing every second of that.”.

LSU head coach Mulkey noted she had “no clue” about what transpired.

Among those defending Reese on social media were ESPN’s Holly Rowe and former NBA star Etan Thomas.

“People hating on Angel Reese or Caitlin Clark. Stop. Unapologetically confident young women should be celebrated NOT hated. Get used to it,” Rowe wrote on Twitter.

It has been revealed that former Washington Wizards, Oklahoma City Thunder and Atlanta Hawks player Thomas wrote: “Hold on now!!!! It was cute when Caitlin Clark did it. Y’all didn’t have any problems with it at all. So don’t be all outraged and talking about class and sportsmanship when Angel Reese does the same thing. We’re not doing double standards here.”.

Reese said the negative reaction on social media throughout the season has helped fuel her excellent season, having finished averaging 23.0 points and 15.4 rebounds in her first season with LSU after transferring from Maryland.

In a recent development, “Twitter can say what they want to say,” she said. “I love reading those comments. I have all the screenshots of what everybody has said about me all season. What are you going to say now?”.

Sources indicate that with a stylish assist and a gorgeous goal, Viktor Gyokeres produced the sort of match-winning performance that suggests the Swedish striker is making significant progress at last. It has not always been straightforward for him at Arsenal, but this was unquestionably one of his better showings, and it continued an encouraging upturn in his form.

Gyokeres has been the second-choice striker for most of this season, with Mikel Arteta usually preferring the more subtle Kai Havertz in attack. There are signs, though, that Gyokeres is now growing in belief. Following this victory over Slavia Prague, which was much more narrow and nervy than it should have been, he has now scored two goals and registered three assists in his last five appearances.

Industry observers note that even more promising than those statistics was his all-round play in Prague. In the first half especially, Gyokeres held on to long passes, combined with his team-mates and tested the opposition with his runs in behind. For Arsenal’s first goal, he found Noni Madueke with a brilliant pass. For their second, he curled a fabulous strike into the top corner.

“Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”.

Sources indicate that those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

Industry observers note that “We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” stated Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”.

Without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

It was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

Industry observers note that the goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

In a recent development, just as Gyokeres is finding his form, so is Madueke. The absence of the injured Bukayo Saka has given Madueke a run in the side and he seems to be benefiting from it, even if he still lacks the same consistency in decision-making as his England team-mate.

One of Slavia’s many problems in a one-sided first half was their inability to cope with Arsenal’s rotations in midfield. Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi and Merino were all alternating positions at will, taking turns to drop deep and push forward. Merino could have scored a couple, before he combined sharply with Gyokeres for Arsenal’s second.

It has been revealed that gyokeres has never been the most delicate link-up player, and there have been too many times when the ball has simply bounced off him, but here he was impressively sleek. A quick exchange of passes with Merino allowed him a sight of goal, and the curled finish was sumptuous. For a man known for his power, this was an uncharacteristic demonstration of finesse.

Game over? Arsenal clearly thought so. They certainly came out for the second half like a team that believed the job was done. Arteta became increasingly irate in the first few minutes after the restart, with Ben White on the receiving end of one verbal slap. Rice also received a telling-off, and a yellow card, from the referee after kicking the ball away in annoyance.

Industry observers note that would Slavia have secured a draw if they had been at full strength? They had been weakened by the banishment of their star striker from the club because of a series of disciplinary failings. Tomás Chory, the top scorer for the past two seasons, was chucked out of the team after showing his middle finger to the referee in a recent game. This sort of sanction would have earned Arteta’s approval, no doubt, but it did not increase Slavia’s chances of hurting the Premier League champions in those edgy final few minutes.

Perhaps they will reflect on that decision differently now, given the uncharacteristically wobbly second-half performance by Arsenal. The visitors were vulnerable in the latter stages, when they lacked the control and composure that Arteta expects. Gabriel, too, appeared dismayed by what he was seeing. At one point, he put his hands on his hips and scowled at his team-mates like an angry teacher.

In a recent development, with only a few minutes remaining, Nowak converted a left-wing cross to plunge Arsenal into a proper panic. It required a backs-to-the-wall defensive action, similar to the victory against Liverpool on Sunday, to get over the line.

Industry observers note that always we need to value winning away in the Champions League. It is extremely difficult. Two very different halves. We should have had three or four goals in the first half but we didn’t do it. Right at the start of the second half we were on the back foot, very sloppy and gave balls away. Then we had to suffer. A lot to learn.

We should have scored more in the first half and if we didn’t do that we had to go and do that in the second half.

According to recent reports, we made six changes but we know the quality of the players we have. Whether we were lacking something I don’t know but I would have done the same thing [again].

I value what the team has done now, it is 11 away games we played, but our standards should be higher.

Arteta on Gyokeres: "He was really good. A game we believed was good for him, for the spaces he could use. He was really connected to the team. Great news because I think he needed that. Really pleased.".

In a recent development, arteta: "Two very different halves. The first we played at a really high level. At half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning we were extremely far from our standards. Very far from the standards we expect from each other.".

It has been revealed that first half we played really, really well. We created a lot of chances and could have scored more but the second half was completely different. They stepped up a gear and made it difficult for us and we have to learn from it. Delighted with the win but a lot of things to improve going forward.

Maybe they started pressing a bit higher with more intensity. We had too many giveaways especially in the final third. There was too much running from box to box and we have to manage those reactions and go for the third and fourth goal.

At the end of the day it is three points.

Slavia Prague managed just one shot on goal in the first half worth 0.12 xG but finished the game with 18 shots on Arsenal’s goal and 2.23 xG. Arsenal could easily have dropped points on the balance of the second 45 minutes.

Quite surprised Declan Rice stayed on the pitch for the full 90 minutes there. He seemed to be in a bit of discomfort after a couple of long sprints. And then he got the silly yellow. Arteta perhaps panicking about the result.

Slavia Prague XI: Domchak, Holes, Zima, Vlcek, Suleiman, Moses, Sadilek, Kubiak, Ayaosi, Sturm, Nowak.

Good evening from a chilly Prague, where Arsenal are looking for a repeat of the 3-0 victory they secured here exactly one year ago. It’s a remarkable coincidence that Mikel Arteta’s team have travelled to face Slavia Prague on November 4th in back-to-back years.

On that occasion last year, Max Dowman became the youngest player in Champions League history. He should get more minutes tonight from the bench, given that he is right now suspended from Premier League action following his controversial red card against Fleetwood last week.

It has been revealed that that’s the most Arteta has rotated between a Premier League and Champions League game so far this season. Telling perhaps that Konsa, Gabriel and Rice – the team’s defensive bedrock – stay in place. But changes on both sides at full-back, and in the attacking midfield areas.

Arsenal XI: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Zubimendi, Merino; Madueke, Gyokeres, Eze.

Subs: Kepa, Meslier, Saliba, Mosquera, Timber, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard, Guimaraes, Tzolis, Dowman, Havertz.

Arsenal’s critics will still grumble about the style of victory, but, of all clubs, this is a team who have no obligation to play in a way that neutrals might enjoy. Arsenal spent so much of Arsene Wenger’s 22-year reign playing football that was mostly stylish but only sometimes effective in major games. Now they are mostly effective but only occasionally stylish on such occasions. If you asked all the travelling fans at Anfield which they prefer, you would receive an overwhelming response.

In a recent development, david Raya has kept a clean sheet in 54% of his Champions League starts (21 clean sheets from 39 starts), the best ratio of any goalkeeper to start at least 25 games in the competition. 🤯🇪🇸 https://t.co/A1Zpn8kJN9.

Arsenal return to Slavia Prague for the third time under Mikel Arteta knowing that three points will be another step towards a top-eight finish in the Champions League league phase.

Arteta’s team were 4-0 winners in the Czech capital in a 2021 Europa League quarter-final second leg, and 3-0 victors at this stage of the Champions League a year ago. Bukayo Saka opened the scoring with a penalty before two second-half goals from Mikel Merino.

Paris-St Germain are top of the table on 12 points after their rout against Villarreal last night. Real Madrid, Liverpool and Real Betis are the three teams who have the chance to join them on maximum points. Arsenal will jump to 10 points with a win, above Bayern Munich, Sporting and Aston Villa at a minimum.

Slavia Prague are top of the Czech league and unbeaten after 13 games this season, but they are winless in the Champions League after fixtures against Lens, Sabah and Fernerbahce.

The fixture should be a presentable opportunity for Arteta to rotate his team, especially after a physically taxing game at Anfield where Arsenal revealed their mettle to win at Liverpool’s home for the first time since 2012.

Arsenal’s second-string is very strong, though they did not cover themselves in glory at Fleetwood in the League Cup last week when Max Dowman was sent off. Given the 16-year-old is banned for another two Premier League games, and the attention Arteta’s touchline reaction to the red card attracted, one wonders if he might want to seize a chance to put Dowman back on the horse.

It has been revealed that william Saliba’s return to full training is very welcome news, despite Ezri Konsa impressing in his absence. Saliba travelled with the squad to Prague, and could make his first appearance of the season following a back injury which flared up in France’s World Cup semi-final against Spain. With fixtures against Manchester City, Borussia Dortmund, Brentford, Spurs, Real Madrid, Bournemouth and Manchester United before the end of 2026 though, they will not want rush him.

Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Eberechi Eze are other players pushing for greater involvement from the start of matches.

Tech Report: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, regina Sluszny makes her way in her wheelchair through the iron gate marking the entrance to the former Auschwitz concentration camp.
  • Six, seven, perhaps eight, she estimates.
  • Regina Sluszny traveled to Poland with a delegation from the European Jewish Association (EJA), a European advocacy group representing Jewish interests that regularly organizes conferences on Jewish life as well as visits to former concentration camps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, regina Sluszny makes her way in her wheelchair through the iron gate marking the entrance to the former Auschwitz concentration camp. "I feel the cold, both physically and emotionally," says the 87-year-old Jewish woman, her gaze fixed on the grey horizon.

How many times has she been here? Six, seven, perhaps eight, she estimates. And each time, the same thoughts run through her mind: "I think about my husband's family. He lost seven loved ones here. They were sent straight to the gas chambers and murdered.".

Regina Sluszny traveled to Poland with a delegation from the European Jewish Association (EJA), a European advocacy group representing Jewish interests that regularly organizes conferences on Jewish life as well as visits to former concentration camps.

This year, the organization invited political representatives and members of Jewish communities to Krakow and Auschwitz on November 9 and 10. The trip was deliberately scheduled to coincide with the anniversary of the November Pogroms of 1938, widely regarded as a watershed moment on the path to the Holocaust.

Industry observers note that "Honoring the past, securing the future" is the event's motto. Like many others in attendance, Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny fears that the horrors of the Shoah are slowly fading from Europe's collective memory.

Among this year's international religious and political representatives, the guest of honor was Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran's last shah and a prominent opponent of the Islamic Republic. The European Jewish Association (EJA) honored him for his efforts to combat antisemitism.

Accepting the award, Pahlavi recalled the historic ties between the Persian and Jewish peoples and called on democratic nations around the world to unite against oppression and ideological extremism.

But talking to attendees at the symposium in Krakow, it rapidly becomes clear that fear of rising antisemitism is much closer to home. Many describe growing hostility towards Jews and rising fear in Jewish communities across Europe.

It has been revealed that in France, authorities recorded a total of 1,320 antisemitic incidents in 2025. That was fewer than in 2024, but around three times as many as in 2022.

It has been revealed that in Germany, the number of antisemitic crimes recorded by police rose from 2,641 in 2022 to 6,236 in 2024 and 6,548 in 2025. Authorities and monitoring organizations across Europe have reported a significant increase in antisemitic incidents since October 7, 2023.

Recent findings suggest that for Ellen van Praagh, chair of the Interprovincial Rabbinate in the Netherlands, October 7, 2023, marked a turning point. She also lost a family member during the Hamas-led attack which saw around 1,200 people in Israel killed and over 250 taken hostage and abducted to the Gaza Strip.

Industry observers note that "My family has lived in the Netherlands since the 16th century. And now I'm being told to leave," says van Praagh. She says the atmosphere in the Netherlands has changed dramatically since the attack. She no longer feels safe there as a Jew. "We Jews are being held responsible for Israel's actions.".

Israel released a major military offensive in the Gaza Strip after the October-7 attack. More than 75,000 Palestinians have been killed there since the start of the war, according to conservative estimates.

In a recent development, like many others at the symposium, van Praagh states she is increasingly losing faith in politicians. "Never Again" has become an empty phrase, she argues, with little relevance to the everyday lives of Jews in Europe.

Sources indicate that jewish communities now have to protect themselves behind high walls. Constant security measures restrict their daily lives, she explains. "That is not what we want. We want to live in freedom.".

Sources indicate that rabbi Menachem Margolin, chairman of the European Jewish Association, is also calling on European political leaders to take greater responsibility. He notes he is grateful for their support, without which Jewish life in Europe would hardly be possible.

However, laws designed to protect Jewish life are often not enforced in practice. Many officials hesitate to call antisemitism by its name as soon as doing so becomes politically inconvenient. "But Auschwitz did not begin with gas chambers. It began with words," he cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, regina Sluszny joined the delegation visiting the Birkenau memorial. The Auschwitz concentration and extermination camp, built by Nazi Germany, became a symbol of the Holocaust. The Nazis murdered around 1.1 million people there, including approximately one million Jews. Most were killed here at Birkenau.

The delegation is gathered to commemorate the November Pogroms of November 9 and 10, 1938, when Nazis set synagogues on fire, ransacked Jewish businesses and homes and murdered Jews. Around 30,000 Jewish men were deported to concentration camps.

Survivors like Regina are increasingly rare. Most Holocaust survivors have passed away. Regina survived because, in 1942, a family friend and his wife took her in when she was just two years old while her parents fled the Nazis with her two brothers and went into hiding.

For more than 40 years, she has been sharing her story with schoolchildren, doing her part to ensure that the Holocaust is never forgotten. For her, "Never Again" is a promise that must be kept. Otherwise, it becomes a lie.

This article was originally published in German.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the biggest roster of the year for the U.S.
  • In a recent development, the tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play.
  • In just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the biggest roster of the year for the U.S. women's national team is here. Head coach Emma Hayes has named a 23-player roster for the upcoming 2026 Concacaf W Championship.

In a recent development, the tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play. Fans can watch all the Concacaf W Championship matches on Paramount+.

In just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round. The U.S. and Canada earned direct byes into the tournament as Concacaf's top two ranked teams, and six teams now join them after a preliminary qualifying round. The USWNT will face El Salvador on Nov. 27 in the quarterfinal round, and if they advance, they'll clinch a spot in next year's World Cup. The other matchups are Canada against Panama, Mexico vs. Haiti, and Jamaica will play Costa Rica.

"It's been a great year of growth and learning for our team, and for a long time the focus has been on qualifying for the World Cup, so now that time has arrived," mentioned Hayes.

Sources indicate that "I want to see relentless consistency from our players, individually and as a team, and I want us to be elite in both penalty boxes. If we can achieve that, I'm confident those performances will carry us through to meet our standards and goals. This is my first Concacaf event and the first for many of our players, so we're all looking forward to the experience.".

It has been revealed that hayes selected a full roster that features several players competing in their first-ever senior-level World Cup qualifying tournament, and a handful of veterans. Just eight of the 23 players selected were members of the 2022 Concacaf W Championship roster: forwards Mallory Swanson, Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson, and Ashley Sanchez; defender Emily Fox; and midfielders Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle, and Sam Coffey -- who joined mid-tournament that year.

Coffey returns to the roster after missing two previous international windows while managing a lower-leg injury. Defender Naomi Girma is out as she continues to manage a lingering calf injury. The centerback has not featured with the national team since April, and has yet to play with Chelsea FC this season. Midfielder Olivia Moultrie is currently rehabbing from an ACL injury sustained in August. Other notable omissions on the roster are Jaedyn Shaw and Ally Sentnor, both of whom have been part of U23 and senior camps throughout the year.

Recent findings suggest that this is just the third camp for the attacking line of "triple espresso" since the 2024 Olympics. If the trio starts a match during the Concacaf W Championship, it will be the first time they start a game together since the gold medal match. Both Swanson and Wilson have worked their way back into senior camps over the year following maternity leave.

Listed by position (club; caps/goals).

Goalkeepers (3): Claudia Dickey (Seattle Reign FC; 12/0), Mandy McGlynn (Utah Royals FC; 6/0), Phallon Tullis-Joyce (Manchester United, ENG; 8/0).

Defenders (8): Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC; 72/3), Kate Del Fava (Utah Royals FC; 1/0), Emily Fox (Arsenal FC, ENG; 80/1), Avery Patterson (Houston Dash; 15/1), Tara Rudd (Washington Spirit; 12/0), Evelyn Shores (Angel City FC; 0/0), Gisele Thompson (Angel City FC; 12/0), Kennedy Wesley (San Diego Wave FC; 9/1).

Midfielders (6): Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current; 7/1), Sam Coffey (Manchester City, ENG; 46/5), Lindsey Heaps (Denver Summit FC; 180/40), Claire Hutton (Bay FC; 22/1), Rose Lavelle (Gotham FC; 124/29), Lily Yohannes (OL Lyonnes, FRA; 22/1).

Forwards (6): Michelle Cooper (Kansas City Current; 16/1), Trinity Rodman (Washington Spirit; 59/13), Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage; 30/4), Mallory Swanson (Chicago Stars; 105/39), Alyssa Thompson (Chelsea FC, ENG; 34/4), Sophia Wilson (Portland Thorns FC; 65/25).

In a recent development, ashley Sanchez's return to the roster comes after standout performances against Spain last window and a stellar 2026 NWSL regular season where she won the Golden Boot with 20 goals scored. She was also nominated for the 2026 NWSL MVP award. A positional shift to left winger and an outrageous amount of scoring have all led her back to the USWNT due to consistent performances, a key factor for Hayes with her large player pool.

In a recent development, "Be consistent first of all in performance. Ashley Sanchez wasn't on our radar, not because she isn't talented, but there were certain things we demanded from the performance that I think she has delivered in her game on a regular basis. So, I think that's the first thing. I think you've seen that includes Croix Bethune coming into this camp -- been outstanding in the number 10 position all year, and would have been in last camp as well if she was fit. You do have to consistently find consistent performances, particularly if you're a player that doesn't have credit in the bank," Hayes mentioned.

Industry observers note that as the World Cup gets nearer, finalizing a roster for the 2027 summer tournament is even closer. Things like consistent form and senior-level experience will come into play when naming a final 23 for the World Cup for Hayes.

Industry observers note that "If you're a Mallory Swanson and delivered on a world stage on a regular basis for the national team, it does alter things slightly. No, we don't want players that are in our group that are in a place where they're not fighting to improve every day or be as competitive as they could possibly be, but I think when players have stacked and accumulated a lot of experience over a period of time, that is always going to put them in a steady position," Hayes explained.

According to recent reports, "But it doesn't guarantee anything. I will be unafraid to leave anybody off that plane if I don't feel that they are applying themselves to put ourselves in the best possible position to compete. Which is why this upcoming camp, our job is to qualify for the World Cup, and so everything we have worked towards is ensuring that every player that comes in at camp makes sure they lift their level and they position the team to have the most positive outcome, regardless of the opponent. And I'd be demanding as much as I always do, but I have a major expectation from our senior players to step up.".

Recent findings suggest that el Salvador is the eighth-ranked team in the Concacaf W Championship and earned its spot following a preliminary qualifying round. The group is coached by manager Eric Acuña, who recently made headlines for harshly criticizing his players in a press conference following losses to Paraguay last month.

Still, Hayes and the staff aren't taking any opponent lightly no matter the rankings or state of the locker room.

"It's a team that knows is competing for something, so it doesn't matter the opponent; they're competing to go to a World Cup, and do I think that will be it will be demanding and taxing? And yes, I do. In many different ways, because the expectations are all on us. I think for them, it's how are they going to disrupt us and make it difficult? But they have two players in the front line that can cause a lot of problems, particularly in transition. So we have to set up for that," Hayes remarked.

"I think when it when it comes to the players, I've always championed creating positive environments for players. And yeah, I'm sad for the players to hear what they've gone through, but as always, I can't control that. I want the best for players all of the time in their environments, but I am here to represent the U.S. and try and help us qualify for the World Cup. So my focus is on that. Even if my heart goes out to the players and I think we still have a lot of work to do in the women's game to keep driving female-centered, female-lens environments where women can thrive.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.
  • Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.

Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.

As a result, UEFA have fined the FA and banned away fans from attending one UEFA match for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.

That said, the ban will only take effect if England supporters reoffend within the next two years.

It is a fortunate reprieve given the Three Lions' next away fixture is their Nations League quarter-final, the draw for which is on Friday.

Meanwhile, the FA have committed to identifying those involved and taking action - which could see football banning orders imposed.

In a statement to Daily Mail Sport, the FA said: 'We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.'.

England fans land FA in hot water over 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' chant during Spain victory.

England supporters have notoriously sung the anti-Catholic and loyalist chant. In 2024, the Irish police urged travelling fans to 'respect local culture' before their Nations League match against the Republic of Ireland.

Fans were also filmed in Milan city centre on the eve of the clash against Italy in 2022 singing the same incendiary chant - just one year after their European Championship final defeat to the Italians.

Meanwhile, then England boss Roy Hodgson and the FA were forced to condemn supporters after the inflammatory chant was heard throughout England's 3-1 friendly victory over Scotland at Celtic Park in 2014. Around 5,000 fans travelled to the devoutly Catholic club.

In a recent development, the glitch is not limited to international football. In August, Daily Mail Sport revealed that Chelsea wrote to supporters after a section of their fans were heard singing the sectarian chant away at Fulham on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was asked about racism in his pre-Spain press conference.

'I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on Earth and that's exactly how it works,' Tuchel remarked.

Industry observers note that 'I expect emotional and of course supporting fans from Spain for their national team. That's what I expect, but I don't expect racism nowhere.

'I'm shocked if it happens, and it should happen nowhere, and I'm the first one to stand up for these kind of values.

'My trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: bring people together and not divide people.'.

#1741. The last golden era of the Premier League is long gone: Why 2004-16 was the best of the Barclays

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1108 w)

The last golden era of the Premier League is long gone: Why 2004-16 was the best of the Barclays

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the so-called “Best League in the World™”, it’s safe to say the Premier League is presently experiencing a full-blown existential crisis.
  • Industry observers note that the bombshell announcement of Manchester City’s guilt on all but one of their 115 charges has left the game feeling more hollow than ever before.
  • So with that, let’s cast our minds to a simpler, purer time, the much-fabled “Barclays era” of 2004 to 2016.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the so-called “Best League in the World™”, it’s safe to say the Premier League is presently experiencing a full-blown existential crisis.

Industry observers note that the bombshell announcement of Manchester City’s guilt on all but one of their 115 charges has left the game feeling more hollow than ever before. Is there a title race? Who’s going down? What is real? Does any of this mean anything? Throw in the continued abomination that is VAR and more, and it’s all just a bit bleak.

So with that, let’s cast our minds to a simpler, purer time, the much-fabled “Barclays era” of 2004 to 2016.

While football didn’t start in 1992, the Premier League did and by the early-to-mid 2000s, it was reaching its apex as the blood and thunder of decades prior fused with the upcoming-found flair and panache to create a near-perfect concoction.

Sources indicate that the current state of the English top-flight can be traced all the way back to the summer of 2003 with Roman Abramovich’s purchase of Chelsea. It was the moment the horse bolted and nothing has been the same since.

In a recent development, however, at the time, it was all just a little bit exciting and things really picked up 12 months later when Jose Mourinho landed in West London, rightly claiming to be the “Special One”. The reigning European Cup winner was joined by Rafael Benitez, who came to Liverpool after incredible success with Valencia.

Suddenly, Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger were no longer the only gunslingers in town. The “Significant Two” quickly became the “Big Four” as Mourinho romped to the league title - breaking numerous records - and Benitez amazingly won the Champions League. Istanbul and all that.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

According to recent reports, the two Iberians changed so much in the English game. From how to set up a side to how to win the title - 4-4-2 and peaking after Christmas being swapped out for 4-3-3 and rapid-fast starts.

Liverpool’s fifth European Cup was significant for numerous reasons. It was their first in 21 years but also the first final featuring an English side in the 21st century. They had beaten Chelsea to get there, starting both an incredible rivalry between the clubs and managers, and a golden age for the Premier League.

According to recent reports, over the next four years, all of the then-”Massive Four” made finals and there were three semi-finalists in every season from 06/07 to 08/09. The peak came in 2008 when each was knocked out by another with United eventually toppling Chelsea in the first all-English final in Moscow. In one of the odder paradoxes, England failed to qualify for the European Championships that summer.

Fergie’s empire had struck back with Cristiano Ronaldo and Wayne Rooney at the forefront of it. In an era of elite pairings, there was no finer. Ronaldo’s Ballon d’Or win confirmed his status as the best player in the world, and the Premier League as truly the best league.

It was also a time of far less financial disparity with the rest of Europe, Milan and Inter lifting the Champions League in 2007 and 2010 respectively. Things would soon change and not for the better.

Recent findings suggest that while the massive boys competed for the biggest trophies, there were plenty of brilliant stories elsewhere. Harry Redknapp’s Portsmouth won the FA Cup in 2008, setting the tone for Wigan five years later in epic fashion against City months on from Swansea claiming the League Cup. Only Crystal Palace's success in 2025 has been comparable since.

Throw in Big Sam’s Bolton, Blackburn, Stoke, Hull and others and it was the last definitive age of the cult teams and cult heroes, or as they’ve become better known - The Barclaysmen. With the overload of data nowadays, another Michu-like madness feels further away than ever.

Abu Dhabi’s takeover of City in 2008 is the obvious place to pinpoint the beginning of the end, but Mourinho’s first Chelsea exit a year prior and Ronaldo’s first from United a year after moved the centre of attention from England to Spain.

Recent findings suggest that while European success faded - a fate-like Chelsea were the only winners from 2008 to 2019 - there were still memorable domestic moments, two of which unfortunately led to City winning their first pair of Premier League titles. Agueroooooo and Gerrard’s slip may be rendered utterly irrelevant soon but the memories won’t. It was peak Premier League.

As was Sir Alex Ferguson’s last dance in 2013 and Leicester’s miracle title win in 2016, which will never be topped as the greatest achievement in the history of English football. That it came either side of Chelsea’s crooked titles and prior to City’s dodgy dominance makes it all the more appropriate as the ending of the last great era. And that goes for both in football and the world itself.

While the on-field action of the last decade may feel fraudulent, how we now consume football is also a far cry from those halcyon Barclays days.

In a recent development, streaming was not yet a thing in 2004. Sky Sports was in its pomp. Super Sunday actually lived up to its billing as appointment viewing.

Influencers and content creators had not yet taken over. Gary Neville went past his winger on the overlap rather than host it. Social media was still fun for the most part.

We had Soccer AM and Goals on Sunday, Gillette Soccer Saturday and Match of the Day at elite levels, and even room for highlights like Wayne Rooney’s Street Striker and Football’s Next Star.

Nostalgia is a helluva drug, but as Independent Panels decide the fate of English football past, present and future, it’s near-impossible to dispute that, like so much of entertainment, we had it so much better before.

One day, the pendulum will hopefully swing back in our favour but, for now, a rewatch of Premier League Years on Sky may be in order.

#1738. Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (719 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (719 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work.
  • Across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often.
  • The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work. But a new study suggests that for women, it can also lead to worse treatment from colleagues.

Across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often. Men with high scores did not receive such treatment, and in one group, they were treated better.

The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.

Industry observers note that since it was published this year, Nitya Chawla, an associate professor at UCL School of Management in London and the researcher behind the study, notes women have written to her saying the findings matched their own experience at work. Some told her they had wondered whether they were to blame for hostility.

In a recent development, the researchers ran two studies. The first followed 432 business students at a US public university working in small teams on a consulting project for real organizations. The second surveyed 394 full-time employees working in teams at a financial organization in China.

Intelligence here means cognitive ability measured with a standardized test of reasoning and problem-solving that employers use in hiring. Teammates were not told of anyone's scores. They rated one another, and a few weeks later each person reported how much help they had received and how often they had been undermined, for instance by having information withheld.

The effects were small, and the study shows a link, not proof that colleagues' perceptions caused the treatment. Participants reported help and mistreatment themselves, and the study did not look at race or ethnicity.

In the student group, the difference between women and men was no longer statistically significant when two participants with extremely low scores were included.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that the researchers point to social role theory, the idea that people expect men and women to fit traditional roles: men as capable and assertive, women as warm and supportive. A woman with high cognitive ability breaks that expectation, and colleagues may assume she lacks warmth.

"It's that automatic, implicit assumption that takes place alongside the presence of intelligence that then drives these more negative interpersonal behaviors," Chawla told DW.

In a recent development, in both groups, women with higher scores were rated as more hostile. Among the employees in China, they were also rated as less warm. Women seen as more hostile reported less help, both with their work and on a personal level, and more undermining.

Industry observers note that the team also checked whether the women were simply behaving differently. Higher-scoring women were rated as somewhat more domineering, but that did not explain why they received less help or more mistreatment. The findings point to colleagues' assumptions, Chawla says, rather than to anything the women did.

No, men with high intelligence scores do not face the same treatment. Among the students in the United States, a man's score made no difference to how his teammates rated or treated him.

Among the employees in China, men with higher scores were rated as less hostile, received more help and were mistreated less often. The authors suggest the difference between the two groups may reflect cultural differences in gender norms, but they did not test this.

In a recent development, no, Chawla states. "That would be really the wrong conclusion to draw.".

Sources indicate that small effects still matter, she argues, because they are experienced day after day. Over time, this kind of treatment can lead to anxiety, self-doubt and a sense of not belonging. "These experiences and these feelings can become very, very burdensome over time," she noted.

Chawla puts the responsibility on workplaces rather than on women. Managers, she says, should track how team members treat one another, and organizations should hold regular check-ins to see whether employees are getting equal support.

Individuals can ask themselves a simple question, she states: would they react the same way if that colleague were a man?
