Why U.S. Soccer's move to name Emma Hayes to the USMNT hiring committee makes sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.
  • Recent findings suggest that men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that WASHINGTON, D.C. – By the time U.S. Soccer confirmed Mauricio Pochettino's departure for Manchester United early Friday morning, the announcement itself was far from a surprise. The press release included the usual formalities – Steve Cherundolo, the U-23 U.S. men's national team head coach, would fill in for the Dec. 13 friendly against Jamaica that falls outside the FIFA international match calendar, and the assurance that the search for Pochettino's USMNT successor would begin shortly. Federation CEO J.T. Batson and COO Dan Helfrich will unsurprisingly lead the search, as will "the soccer leadership team at U.S. Soccer that includes" assistant sporting director Oguchi Onyewu. There was one unique detail tucked into the announcement, though.

Emma Hayes, the U.S. women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.

Recent findings suggest that men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event. They operate on different calendars and in the best case scenarios, each team has dedicated members of staff. Hayes' name-drop as news of Pochettino's exit became official, then, is a unicorn-like sighting, even if U.S. Soccer often champions a spirit of collaboration between all of its national teams. It is uncommon for the head coach of one senior national team to help recruit a counterpart but in U.S. Soccer's case, it makes complete sense.

Recent findings suggest that hayes' coaching career, which spans two decades and two continents, means her inclusion on the federation's soccer leadership team is an obvious one. She is amongst the most respected soccer minds in the game, which easily makes her one of the most notable people on U.S. Soccer's payroll no matter how you look at it. That will be especially true in a hiring process that has to conclude with a compelling follow-up act to Pochettino's splashy arrival two years ago. Her perspective might actually be vital in the process, which only adds to the intrigue of what's next for the USMNT.

It has been revealed that "We have an extraordinary gift, which is a women's national team manager who's incredibly insightful, bright mind about the sport, who has a set of personal experiences and relationships that span the club and international game, the men's and women's game, the domestic and international club game, and who also has lived in the shoes of what it's like to be a U.S. national team senior coach," Helfrich told CBS Sports on Thursday. "It is a no-brainer that that mind and that voice has a really prominent seat at the table when we're talking about key moves for the federation.".

In a recent development, USMNT coaches are rarely style hires; look no further than the list of people to hold the job on a full-time basis this century and the picture paints itself. The only thing Bruce Arena, Bob Bradley, Jurgen Klinsmann, Gregg Berhalter and Pochettino seem to have in common, outside of the job they all once held, is that they were all tasked with some sort of cultural reset depending on the task at hand. That likely will not be the case for Pochettino's successor, though, who will inherit a team with a clear style of play, a healthy mix of veteran players and rising talents and plenty of time on the clock until the next World Cup. The job will be defined in part by continuity, even with the necessary allowance for the new hire to put their unique spin on things.

Industry observers note that that's where Hayes' expertise should play a crucial role, and the same goes for Onyewu. Hayes' tactical know-how makes her as qualified as anyone employed by U.S. Soccer to establish the right stylistic profile for the next USMNT coach, especially with the spirit of continuity in mind. Pochettino's track record with the U.S. team was mixed but at its best, his high-intensity, attack-minded approach suited the player pool really well and continues to do so. Hayes, a tactical pragmatist who prioritized attack-minded teams herself with Chelsea and the USWNT, will be more than able to help match candidates to the player pool they will spend the next several years working with. Hayes admitted as much on Wednesday when addressing the topic for the first time.

According to recent reports, "I work really closely with J.T. in particular and even more so with Dan as we're growing to develop the American soccer movement and J.T. asked if I would be involved as a technical voice, to be involved with the process and I feel confident in the group of people that have been put together to create a thorough process to select the next men's national team coach," she mentioned. "My role is merely to support that through a technical lens, knowing I do this job, albeit with the women's team, and that I've coached for a number of years and can offer some of that insight into the application of what to look for and why and like I said, I feel confident in the group that are being put together. I think it'll be a very thorough process. I think that's the most key part of it and like I said, I feel very embedded in what we're doing with the federation so it doesn't feel unusual to me so, like I've said many times, let's build off the good work that Mauricio has done. I think that's the important part and let's get it right.".

Industry observers note that that's especially true considering the fact that there are very few slam-dunk candidates to replace Pochettino. Pep Guardiola, months into a sabbatical after a decade with Manchester City, is an obvious target for U.S. Soccer but it is entirely unclear how interested he would be in the vacancy. If he's out of the running, the list of contenders with genuine international appeal dwindles promptly but it does not necessarily mean the list of worthy candidates vanishes with Guardiola. The hiring committee will need to be strategic in that case, both in terms of creating a list of contenders and then narrowing them down over the interview process, Hayes providing an key perspective along the way.

The jobs of the USMNT and the USWNT head coaches are hardly apples-to-apples but even then, one will still have an acute idea of what the other's job entails. There is inherent value in having a coach help in the process of hiring another coach, since they hold such singular positions – they are often treated as the be-all, end-all when it comes to their team's success, fairly or otherwise. She can also speak to the cadence of national teams, which varies greatly from the club game where coaches essentially work with their players every day during a long season.

"Everyone is aware of the major differences between coaching at the club level and international level, and the main difference is just time on the field and time with your players," Hayes told CBS Sports earlier this year when asked about Pochettino. "Every international coach would love to have more time with their team, but that's not the nature of the international calendar and it's something I know we both had to get used to and are still getting used to … I noted a few times that it's almost like we are grandparents. We get to see the players for a week or so and then we send them back to their parents, which is their clubs.".

Outside of her tactical expertise, though, Hayes represents U.S. Soccer's ambitious turn in recent years as much as Pochettino does. She was hired because of her reputation as a serial winner at Chelsea, where she won eight league titles and seven cups. She continued the trend in short order with the USWNT – two months after officially starting in the role, she won Olympic gold at the Paris Games in 2024. U.S. Soccer has equally ambitious goals for the men's team, though the timeline will understandably be longer for that program. They continue to target the USMNT's first World Cup quarterfinal appearance since 2002 but in between, they also hope to medal in the Olympics' men's soccer event, which is contested by U-23 teams, for the first time when the Games come to Los Angeles in 2028. More than many at the federation, Hayes has experience with the intangibles it takes to reach those heights and that's exactly why she was hired in the first place. It also reflects what U.S. Soccer's executives are looking for in the next USMNT head coach.

"The most important characteristic is someone with ambition that matches ours, which is high and so when you have, then, that high shared ambition, then you look for the experience, the talent, the understanding that accompanies that ambition," Helfrich said.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, though, Hayes in particular has an idea of what the USMNT job might entail. She is the best of both worlds – she began her coaching career in the U.S. two decades ago and has a deep understanding of the American soccer landscape, but made a name for herself in her native England and can also bring a useful outsider's perspective. There is no perfect equivalent to Hayes waiting for the USMNT job since no coach with experience in the American game has truly broken into the top tiers of the sport just yet, the federation likely to settle for one or the other. Hayes' understanding of both orbits, though, makes her an vital guiding force along the way. She might be the only qualified person to answer how much to weigh the insider's perspective with the accomplished outsider's point of view when looking for the next USMNT head coach, in large part because she is the only person who boasts an equal share of it.

According to recent reports, hayes' expertise alone means she will be as valuable a sounding board as any, to the point that it's hard to minimize her ability to offer input down to one or two straightforward things. There is one more thing Hayes might have that no one at U.S. Soccer does – easy access to some of the most notable coaches in the game.

Industry observers note that over the course of her successful 12-year tenure at Chelsea, Hayes became one of the most respected coaches in England. She became the first woman to win the Football Writers Association's Tribute Award in 2024 shortly before leaving England for the U.S., and has earned the praise of many of her counterparts in the men's game along the way. Out of anyone at U.S. Soccer, Hayes might actually have the most compelling list of phone numbers in her contacts. She has stated Sir Alex Ferguson, a coaching legend if there ever was one after his storied 27-year tenure at Manchester United, calls her "from time to time." Hayes has been in touch with a handful of her contemporaries over the years, including those who have been on U.S. Soccer's radar at one point or another. In her 2024 book, "A Completely Different Game," Hayes said she heard from Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp after having an emergency hysterectomy because of endometriosis in 2022. The pair "sent me long messages, expressing deeply felt emotions," as did Graham Potter and David Moyes.

The rolodex is a covetable one, if ex-U.S. Soccer sporting director Matt Crocker can serve as an example. His greatest accomplishments during his three-year spell, which came to an end in April when he took a similar role with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation, were hiring Hayes and Pochettino. He had previously worked with Pochettino at Southampton a decade earlier, which made U.S. Soccer's approach easier when discussions started. Hayes' value exceeds her ability to hand her bosses a phone number but it is unlikely to go unnoticed at U.S. Soccer, who clearly understands the expertise she would bring to the search in a variety of ways.

#1735. The summer that changed Welsh football

The summer that changed Welsh football

📅 04 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Walking to the ground in Bordeaux and what I find hilarious, in hindsight, is how low our expectations were.".
  • Wales had gone more than half a century without playing at a major tournament, so it was understandable that expectations were modest.
  • Generations of fans had been scarred by agonising near misses and downright dismal failures of the past so, when Wales finally realised a nation's dream by qualifying for Euro 2016, just being there was enough for many.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Walking to the ground in Bordeaux and what I find hilarious, in hindsight, is how low our expectations were.".

Wales had gone more than half a century without playing at a major tournament, so it was understandable that expectations were modest.

Generations of fans had been scarred by agonising near misses and downright dismal failures of the past so, when Wales finally realised a nation's dream by qualifying for Euro 2016, just being there was enough for many.

Bordeaux was bathed in sunshine on the afternoon of Saturday, 11 June, tens of thousands of Welsh supporters descending on the French city for their opening game against Slovakia.

Sources indicate that "We were all saying things like, 'Oh, the anthem's going to be good, that's guaranteed'. We could have lost 10-0 but they were definitely playing the anthem," the comedian and presenter tells BBC Sport Wales as part of Iconic: The Summer that Changed Welsh Football.

Industry observers note that an anthem heard at a major tournament for the first time in 58 years. Glorious catharsis to stir the soul.

Wales had ridden a wave of emotion to get there, a golden generation of players - Gareth Bale, Aaron Ramsey et al - scaling new heights under the guidance of their charismatic manager Chris Coleman.

"I was saying to all the players, 'Keep calm, don't act like we're too excited to be here'," Coleman recalls.

Sources indicate that "But Bordeaux was like the centre of Cardiff, Welsh fans everywhere outside the hotel and, as soon as we were getting on the bus, I was chanting with the fans! I was like, 'What am I doing? Calm down'. I got lost in it.".

In a recent development, coleman and his players eventually composed themselves. After a trademark Bale free-kick had put Wales in front, Hal Robson-Kanu came off the bench to score a late winner and send a nation into raptures.

"Euro 2016 was a turning point for Welsh football," claims Ben Davies, the Tottenham Hotspur defender who made a crucial goalline block early in the game.

"There was so much talk about 1958 and I'd heard about it, I'd seen the odd clip about it, but it felt like a pipedream to actually have Wales in a major tournament.

"So to do it, forget about how well we did in it, just to even get to that tournament, it gave us a belief that it was possible.".

For those among the sea of red shirts in Bordeaux that day, it did not feel like life could get any better - but this was only the beginning.

This was the summer that would change Welsh football forever.

âIt was like being in the centre of Cardiff â there were Welsh fans everywhereâ.

Until Euro 2016, Wales' story had been dominated by tales of heartache, Joe Jordan's handball in 1977 and the Romania defeat of 1993 among many painful chapters.

But by getting to France, Wales freed themselves from that history.

"There had been some really low points for Wales, so to finally do that was a huge achievement," indicates Ramsey, the then Arsenal midfielder who would go on to be named in Uefa's team of the tournament.

Wales had momentum they had never felt before coming into the competition. Victory over Slovakia - and the prospect of getting to the second round - took that to another level.

A last-gasp defeat by England in Lens momentarily punctured that optimism, but the final group game against Russia presented Coleman's side with a chance to secure their place in the knockout stages.

This was meant to be nerve-wracking for a team with no major tournament experience against seasoned opponents.

But under a lilac sunset in Toulouse, Coleman's men played with a flair and verve unlike any other Wales side.

It has been revealed that "That was our best performance," says Coleman. "We were awesome.".

Wales cut Russia to ribbons with a breathtaking attacking display, racing into a 2-0 lead in 20 minutes.

After Ramsey's delicate finish put Wales in front, they poured forward with such gusto that even Neil Taylor scored - the wing-back's first goal since he was playing in non-league for Wrexham six years earlier.

"When Tayls scored, that summed up how things were falling for us," says Joe Allen, who was exceptional in midfield that night.

"This was one of those once-in-a-lifetime moments you've got to capitalise on.".

That is exactly what Wales did. Bale added a third in the second half to become the tournament's top scorer at that point, and the winning margin could have been even wider.

Joe Ledley (right) dances in front of the Wales fans after the 3-0 win over Russia in Toulouse.

"We completely dominated them," states Joe Ledley, who ran the game alongside Allen in midfield.

As well as Ledley played, though, what elevated him to cult status was his post-match dancing in front of the Wales fans.

"I don't know where those moves came from," he grins. "I used to dance with my mates all the time at local pubs in Fairwater [in Cardiff]. I just went for it.".

Wales fans could scarcely believe what they had witnessed. Having already lived a dreamlike existence in France, this was starting to feel surreal.

The odyssey took them to Paris next, Wales' first knockout fixture since Pele had scored the only goal as Brazil beat them in a 1958 World Cup quarter-final.

This time, Coleman's men had the novelty of being favourites against an obdurate Northern Ireland side, who made life difficult for their opponents in a tense last-16 tie.

Bale eventually prised them open â his cross turned into his own net by Gareth McAuley â to set up a quarter-final against Belgium, and what would turn out to be the greatest night in Welsh football history.

'I remember like it was yesterday' - Euro 2016 hero Robson-Kanu.

It has been revealed that wales fans made a lasting impression in France, with their distinctive bucket hats and chant of 'Don't Take Me Home', which became an unofficial anthem of the Euros. Uefa even gave them an "outstanding contribution" award.

"What I loved about Welsh supporters at the Euros was we were just desperate to enjoy every second and suck the marrow out of it because we didn't know if it was going to happen again," notes James.

"We're there to have fun. I'm not saying the result was secondary, but we all had realistic expectations.".

No wonder when you consider Wales' quarter-final opponents were Belgium, ranked number one in the world at the time with a squad boasting stellar talents such as Kevin de Bruyne, Romelu Lukaku and Eden Hazard.

"That Belgian side, on paper, was like a team to represent Earth against Mars," James adds. "It was like a team from space.".

It did not help matters that the game was essentially a home fixture for Belgium, whose fans filled the stadium in Lille, fewer than 10 miles from the Belgian border.

The odds were stacked against Coleman and his players, lengthening further when Radja Nainggolan's thunderous long-range strike gave Belgium an early lead.

But Wales believed they could win, not least because they had beaten Belgium in a qualifier in Cardiff 13 months earlier, and they responded magnificently as captain Ashley Williams headed in a deserved equaliser.

Then, nine minutes into the second half, Bale played a raking long ball to Ramsey, who found Robson-Kanu in the penalty area. And time stood still.

Recent findings suggest that "I remember controlling the ball in the box and there was momentum carrying everyone away from the goal," Robson-Kanu says. "I just remember Cruyffing the entire opposition.".

With a manoeuvre as audacious as it was inspired, Robson-Kanu flummoxed three surrounding Belgian defenders with a Cruyff-turn before finishing supremely beyond Thibaut Courtois.

Wales' fans came to be known as the Red Wall during Euro 2016.

"It was an out-of-body experience," adds the forward, who was without a club at the time.

"Looking back, you realise careers are defined by moments, and to have a moment that you're truly remembered for is a real honour.".

According to recent reports, belgium pushed desperately for an equaliser but Sam Vokes headed in superbly to seal a 3-1 triumph. The celebrations were as ecstatic on the touchline as they were in the stands; disbelief as it dawned on players, staff and fans that Wales were heading to their first semi-final.

"There are certain moments in your life that are so good you wish you could just stop it and say, 'Let's just sit in this moment'," indicates Coleman.

"That was one of those moments. We got back in the dressing room and I can't describe the atmosphere.".

Allen, another Welshman in Uefa's team of the tournament, adds: "That's the moment where it crossed from being a good story into, 'This is more than anyone dreamed was possible'.".

The next, and what would prove to be the final, stop on Wales' magical ride was a semi-final against eventual champions Portugal in Lyon.

Shorn of the suspended Ramsey and Davies, Wales were stifled by their canny opponents, who secured a 2-0 win with second-half goals from Cristiano Ronaldo and Nani.

This was the end of the adventure in France, but the beginning of a glorious era for Welsh football.

"It was a really important moment for Wales, our history and generations to come," claims Ramsey.

Having been absent from major tournaments for 58 years, Wales went on to qualify for a second successive European Championship, before achieving what Davies describes as the "holy grail" of reaching a first World Cup for 64 years in 2022.

"We opened the door that had been closed a long time," says Coleman.

The milestones kept coming, with the women's side qualifying for their first major tournament at Euro 2025.

Whereas Welsh national teams only used to dream of playing on the world's grandest stages, there is now an expectation they get there â and that stems from 2016.

Wales players and staff celebrate with their fans after their Euro 2016 quarter-final win over Belgium.

"With more money coming in from qualification for the European Championships, particularly Euro 2016, we ended up being more cash-rich," indicates Jonathan Ford, chief executive of the Football Association of Wales (FAW) from 2009 to 2021.

In a recent development, "That enabled us to put more money across the board: women's football, grassroots football. We transformed the women's game.".

Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister is a former captain of Wales who played a leading role in getting the FAW to formally establish a national women's team in the 1990s.

"There was nothing inevitable about what happened post-2016 and that's why I think we should give credit to the FAW, and Jonathan Ford particularly, for steering us out of the tournament into that era," claims McAllister.

According to recent reports, "I was part of the FAW Trust in 2016. I can remember times before that when Jonathan came into the board and mentioned things like, 'Until the men qualify for a major tournament, we can't invest in X, Y and Z'. And that included the women's national team.

"While I bristled at that because it felt unfair, the financial realities of the FAW meant until the men got to a position where they generated income from participating and winning, it was going to be impossible for us to deliver the strategy we had for Welsh football.".

McAllister travelled to France 10 years ago as a fan, and Qatar in 2022 to cheer on Wales' men at a World Cup.

When the women played at Euro 2025 in Switzerland, McAllister was there again to see the legacy not only of her own pioneering work in establishing the team but the far-reaching effects of 2016.

It has been revealed that "Something happens when you qualify. It's flicking a switch in mentality - it becomes something realistic and achievable," she adds.

"What matters far more is what you do with the breakthrough moment, not how you've performed.".

Wales' women are now trying to take the next step of qualifying for their first World Cup, while the men looked on enviously as their showpiece event happened without them in the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

Disappointing as it was, that frustration itself represented a shift in mindset that came after Euro 2016 â a sharp contrast to the passive acceptance that met Wales' previous absence from major tournaments.

Since that golden month in France, Wales feel like they belong at this level.

"The best thing we could give the teams coming after us was to say it's possible," says Coleman.

Subsequent qualifications have been the legacy of Euro 2016, while future ambitions are proof of a desire to ensure generations to come continue to build on the foundations laid by their predecessors.

There is plenty more Wales' men and women want to achieve but, whatever happens, there will never be another summer quite like Euro 2016.

"We're so proud of each other and what we achieved," says Ledley.

"Nobody thought we'd do it. When I walk down the street now, everyone says, 'Thank you for 2016, the best summer of my life'.".

James can attest to that. "It remains the best month of my life," he says. "I don't think you often know it's the best month of your life as it's happening.".

With the benefit of hindsight, it is laughable to think you could find a Welsh football fan who would disagree.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway. An awards show, countless events, and media days were all on the agenda ahead of Saturday's big game. That included the annual state of the league by commissioner Jessica Berman on Thursday.

It has been revealed that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m. ET. She also announced a few upcoming league rules and future match events.

Here are the latest things coming to NWSL:.

Industry observers note that the commissioner introduced the newly introduced player development rule. While the league previously submitted paperwork for a potential future second=division league, conversation and planning around that is currently paused with the upcoming 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup and efforts to grow NWSL in other ways.

It has been revealed that "As we grow from 16 to 18 teams in 2028, we know that we have to prioritize the pipeline, not just the pipeline of players, but the pipeline of talent that supports the players in the daily training environment. One of the things that makes the United States so uniquely positioned in the global women's soccer landscape is the depth of that potential pipeline," said Berman in her opening remarks.

It has been revealed that "That's why today we're announcing the NWSL Player Development Rule. It's an important step in strengthening the pathway to professional soccer for the next generation of players. The rule creates actual incentives for clubs to invest in identifying, developing, and retaining young talent, and it gives the clubs the flexibility to design their programs in the way that makes sense with their sporting philosophies.".

More information and the types of incentives will roll out for clubs as the latest player development rule goes into effect, but it is another step in future roster-building for clubs now alongside general player signings, transfers, the High Impact Player rule, and the Under-18 mechanism.

Industry observers note that the addition of the rule is paving the way for more support staff and systems in place. The commissioner also announced the new NWSL Sporting Executive Program, meant to provide more support for club leadership development. The inaugural set of leadership includes six executives from the league who will participate in the program.

Recent findings suggest that "Developing the future of the sport is not just limited to the players; it's also about the technical staff who surround those players each and every day ... this is a first-of-its-kind program invested in talent, and it was curated and developed in collaboration with U.S. Soccer and FIFA. This new year-long initiative will provide sporting executives at our clubs with curated, specialized education, mentorship, and leadership development opportunities tailored around the unique demands of our league and the women's professional game," she noted.

The NWSL commissioner then announced the future site of the next NWSL Challenge Cup. The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup will take place in Austin, Texas, next summer.

The tournament has evolved since its first iteration as a placeholder for the COVID-19-affected season and is now a unique one-off marquee match between top clubs, typically the NWSL Shield titleholders and the NWSL Championship winners. In years where one club wins both, the game is a rematch of the previous NWSL Championship match.

"Following the success of this year's Challenge Cup in Columbus, where we took the event to a neutral site to give an opportunity to introduce the NWSL to a latest community," she mentioned.

The 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup was between 2025 NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current and 2025 NWSL Championship winners Gotham FC. The 2026 competition was held in Columbus, Ohio. The state will now welcome its first NWSL franchise in 2028 alongside another expansion club in Atlanta.

Fans will undoubtedly make the connection and wonder if there is a future where an NWSL club calls Austin home. Right now, there are three NWSL clubs in California and only one in Texas, the Houston Dash.

"We're really excited to create another special experience for our fans and our players while making the NWSL a place that can invite newly introduced audiences," Berman remarked about heading to Austin.

In a recent development, commissioner Berman celebrated the league's recent return to the nation's capital for another NWSL Championship. The city hosted the 2022 event and now returns four years later with more attention on the league, the clubs, and its players than ever before.

Sources indicate that "Today, we're bigger, stronger, more visible, and more ambitious than ever before, and the next five years are going to redefine what's possible. We have an extraordinary opportunity in front of us, and we intend to seize it," she said.

Two incoming clubs set for 2028 and upcoming player roster rules are just the beginning of NWSL's next chapter. There's still the potential for more clubs on the horizon, and current clubs Houston Dash and Racing Louisville are in the process of vetting for a sale to new ownership as franchise entry fees into the league are booming to new heights.

And of course, there is still the biggest game of the year to play on Saturday.

Sources indicate that "The Washington Spirit are back in the championship for the third consecutive year, determined to bring home that title. And standing in their way is the Kansas City Current, with its own ambitions to win a championship after winning the Shield in 2025. These are two exceptional clubs, two incredibly passionate fan base, and the championship is still to be decided, [we're] very excited about the rest of this week.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"It was clear to us from the outset that the analysis would uncover uncomfortable truths," Defence Minister Boris Pistorius of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) told theBundestag, Germany's lower house of parliament, on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that earlier that day, he had presented the findings of the Bundeswehr's first study into unreported cases of sexual misconduct to the Defense Committee. According to the findings, sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known.

"The study has shown that only between one third and one sixth of cases are reported," Pistorius said, announcing an action initiative to address the problem.

Recent findings suggest that "There is zero tolerance for sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr. This is nothing less than a matter of upholding the human dignity enshrined in our Basic Law. And that principle applies all the more within the Bundeswehr.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The study examined incidents that had gone unreported, the so-called "dark figure" of cases that never reach official statistics. The Bundeswehr Centre of Military History and Social Sciences (ZMSBw) surveyed 45,000 service members, around 18% of whom responded. More than 8,100 questionnaires were evaluated and supplemented with individual and group interviews. According to the institute, the data are statistically representative.

According to the study, younger women in the lower ranks are particularly affected by sexual misconduct. Among men, non-heterosexual soldiers are disproportionately affected. The perpetrators are predominantly male. Statistically, combat units do not differ from the rest of the armed forces.

Female service members in units with a higher proportion of women (more than 15%) are less likely to be affected.

Verbal harassment is by far the most common form of misconduct, according to the study. Around 72% of female soldiers and 31% of male soldiers noted they had experienced verbal harassment at least once during their military service. In the 12 months preceding the survey, 38% of female soldiers and 16% of male soldiers reported experiencing verbal sexual harassment.

For physical harassment, 9% of female soldiers and 3% of male soldiers reported incidents of physical sexual misconduct, and 2% of both women and men said they had experienced sexual violence.

The study also examined why service members chose not to report incidents. The most commonly cited reason was not wanting to draw attention to themselves.

Industry observers note that "There appears to be a lack of awareness of the reporting channels. And, for me, the decisive issue is trust in those channels," Pistorius concluded.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In response, the Bundeswehr plans to improve awareness of how and where cases of sexual harassment can be reported. That is precisely where the environmentalist Greens, who are in opposition in the Bundestag, direct their criticism.

Defense policy spokesperson Sara Nanni is calling for "an external reporting office, alongside the regular disciplinary process, with investigative powers and the authority to take disciplinary action where appropriate." Such an independent point of contact, she argues, is needed in cases where superiors within the Bundeswehr fail to fulfill their responsibilities.

Sources indicate that another consequence of the study is the expansion of support services for those affected. A counseling center established in early November will soon be available around the clock. Supervisors are also to receive enhanced awareness training and improved instruction.

"Sexual misconduct will become part of training at every level, from the very beginning," said Bundeswehr Inspector General Carsten Breuer.

Recent findings suggest that in addition, the way supervisors handle reported cases will become a standing criterion in their performance evaluations. "Anyone who fails to lead by example, tolerates misconduct, or does not address it consistently will no longer hold a leadership position," Defense Minister Pistorius stressed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the study was prompted by a growing number of reports of sexual misconduct received by former Parliamentary Commissioner for the Armed Forces Eva Högl. Most of those who approached her were female soldiers. Högl called for the study into unreported cases in 2024. The process gained further momentum following incidents at the Parachute Regiment in Zweibrücken that came to light at the beginning of this year and also involved allegations of sexual misconduct.

It has been revealed that the current Parliamentary Commissioner for the Armed Forces, Henning Otte, described the figures revealed by the study as "dramatically high." The findings had also made it clear, he mentioned, "that there is a lack of trust in the Bundeswehr's structures. The Ministry of Defense must now take this study seriously and translate its findings into a leadership culture that is truly lived in practice.".

The Bundeswehr urgently needs additional personnel and has been actively recruiting women. However, the study's findings are unlikely to make attracting more female recruits any easier. Women remain significantly underrepresented across nearly all branches of the armed forces.

This article was originally written in German.

Chelsea searches for upcoming manager as Premier League breaks record for most sackings in a single season

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It was just six months ago that Graham Potter was deemed the man to usher in a fresh, exciting era at Chelsea.
  • The club’s latest ownership group, led by American businessman Todd Boehly, had enticed Potter away from Brighton with the promise of managing one of the most lucrative teams in world soccer.
  • More than $600 million was spent on bringing major-name players to the club and Potter, one of the most exciting young managers in the Premier League, was to mold them into a winning machine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was just six months ago that Graham Potter was deemed the man to usher in a fresh, exciting era at Chelsea.

The club’s latest ownership group, led by American businessman Todd Boehly, had enticed Potter away from Brighton with the promise of managing one of the most lucrative teams in world soccer.

More than $600 million was spent on bringing major-name players to the club and Potter, one of the most exciting young managers in the Premier League, was to mold them into a winning machine.

Chelsea has spent over $600 million on new signings. Here's why that's significant.

But, on Sunday, the club announced that it had sacked its manager after an underwhelming spell in charge.

Potter managed to win just 10 of the 28 league matches this season and leaves the team 11th in the Premier League table.

In recent weeks, players had looked a shadow of their former selves and many fans had lost confidence that Potter’s blueprint for the club could ever work.

Eventually, after previously sticking by its manager, Blues ownership agreed.

“On behalf of everyone at the club, we want to thank Graham sincerely for his contribution to Chelsea,” the club’s co-owners Todd Boehly and Behdad Eghbali said in a statement.

“We have the highest degree of respect for Graham as a coach and as a person. He has always conducted himself with professionalism and integrity and we are all disappointed in this outcome.”.

In his previous role as Brighton manager, Potter was given time to stamp his identity on the squad.

The club was punching above its weight financially and, as a result, carefully selected new signings which would compliment Potter’s style of play.

The approach paid off as the team became an established Premier League outfit which has gone on to greater things this season – the Seagulls currently sit sixth in the league and in the UEFA Conference League qualification spot.

At Chelsea, it seemed the complete opposite.

As was the case under previous owner Roman Abramovich, the club expected instant results and used its financial weight to sign a number of high-profile names, including the likes of Enzo Fernández and Mykhailo Mudryk.

Despite his impressive CV, Potter had never managed superstars and suddenly found himself in a changing room with multiple.

The scatter gun approach to recruitment also left the team lacking balance and organization with Potter failing to get a tune out of a team busting with talent.

In truth, many had raised an eyebrow when Potter, inexperienced at the very top level, was chosen to replace Thomas Tuchel as manager.

Despite falling out of favor with fans by the end of his tenure, Tuchel had guided Chelsea to the Champions League title in 2021 and is still considered by many as one of the best coaches in the world.

The German has gone on to sign with Bavarian giant Bayern Munich through the 2024/25 season and recently told reporters he needed “quite a bit of time to distance himself from Chelsea” because leaving the club had hurt him.

Bayern Munich sacks manager Julian Nagelsmann, appoints Thomas Tuchel.

“Todd [Boehly] said he would be different to Roman [Abramovich],” former Liverpool player and current pundit Jamie Carragher wrote on Twitter.

“I feel for Graham Potter, but it was inevitable. You don’t change Tuchel for Potter. Ridiculous decision to start with.”.

With 10 games left in the league and a Champions League quarterfinal against Real Madrid on the horizon, Chelsea still has plenty to play for.

Assistant coach Bruno Saltor will take over on an interim basis, but Boehly and his team must now look for a long-term replacement capable – and willing – to bring order to Chelsea’s chaos.

Potter’s sacking is yet another sign of just how transient managers can be in the top-flight of English football, especially when results aren’t instantaneous.

There has now been a record 12 sackings in the Premier League so far this season, with Potter leaving his position the same day Leicester boss Brendan Rodgers was sacked from his.

The previous record was 10 manager changes in a single season, set in four other campaigns, most recently in 2017/18.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 06:33 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 04:07 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to reset the culture at Manchester United as he lifted the lid on being in the stands in 1999 to see the club's greatest triumph.
  • Pochettino was officially appointed as United's new head coach on Wednesday and took charge of training for the first time on Thursday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 06:33 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 04:07 EST, 20 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to reset the culture at Manchester United as he lifted the lid on being in the stands in 1999 to see the club's greatest triumph.

Pochettino was officially appointed as United's new head coach on Wednesday and took charge of training for the first time on Thursday.

The Argentine was pictured greeting his upcoming squad, with several stars having returned from international duty, before attentions turned to preparing the Red Devils for Sunday's trip to Anfield.

Pochettino also addressed the club's internal media team for the first time, outlining how he plans to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most crucial,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

Mauricio Pochettino took Man United first team training for the first time on Thursday.

Matheus Cunha and Lisandro Martinez were among those to report back after international duty.

Man United will hope to hit the ground running under Pochettino when they face Liverpool on Sunday.

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'.

In a recent development, 'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'.

Pochettino's determination to be the man to bring winning football back to Old Trafford is in large part due to one of his founding memories of the club back in 1999 when he was a player at Espanyol.

Alongside his now trusted goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, Pochettino was at the Nou Camp to see United clinch the Champions League, thus sealing a famous Treble, against Bayern Munich.

'In 1999, I was in Barcelona for that final. That was an iconic final,' he added.

'Toni Jimenez [was there] too. We were shouting for Manchester United from there. I was so excited to see Manchester United.

'This [is the] type of game that you stay sitting in your place [for] and you're so excited because you are watching the game. That was an amazing game.

'And then what happened in the end... it's like it's impossible not to empathise with that team, no?

'That was an amazing memory that made me pay more attention to United, to [Sir Alex] Ferguson and the players that were there, that are all legends.'.

That level of success feels a lifetime away from the current squad, which emerges from the international break for a trip to face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield slumped 18th in the Premier League.

Pochettino wants to focus on the potential of his Man United squad, rather than their current Premier League plight.

Pochettino is determined to shift the culture at Manchester United back to winning.

The Argentine head coach was in the stands in Barcelona cheering for United back in 1999.

While there are those who may be daunted trying to turn around the ship which sunk so far it cost Michael Carrick his job, Pochettino wants to focus on potential, rather than the present.

'It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,' a defiant Pochettino added.

In a recent development, 'Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most notable thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure [off].

According to recent reports, 'Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

'When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

'That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

'I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.'.

Pochettino touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning after his overnight flight.

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that pochettino knows that time is not on his side ahead of an upcoming week that sees United travel to face Liverpool on Sunday, followed by a Champions League trip to face Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday. The week is rounded out by a home match a week on Saturday against Brentford.

The Argentine head coach touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning, taking a private jet straight after the final whistle of United States versus Haiti in Cincinnati.

From there he immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff, including Tom Heaton, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Bruno Fernandes. It is understood he left a good first impression on the players.

And yet, in spite of such a packed schedule, which saw him leave Carrington very late at night on Wednesday and reappear bright and early on Thursday for training, Pochettino is raring to go and is eager for his players to head to Anfield on Sunday convinced they can win.

'I have plenty of energy. It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United,' he said.

'And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

'Now it's not time to think about rest, it's not time to think about sleep. It's about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.'.

Life as a Wag in the transfer window

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Owen was on the phone to the manager and his agent while I was in labour.
  • Owen Dale's loan deal wasn't to a local club, but to Portsmouth - a city more than 200 miles away.
  • Industry observers note that and the pair had only just got the keys to a house they had bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Owen was on the phone to the manager and his agent while I was in labour. They waited for me to give birth and then he went out on loan pretty much as soon as I was out of hospital.".

Owen Dale's loan deal wasn't to a local club, but to Portsmouth - a city more than 200 miles away. His partner, Jessica Beaumont, had never even been there.

Industry observers note that and the pair had only just got the keys to a house they had bought. They would end up staying in it for just one night.

"Since living together, we've moved five times in five years," says Jessica.

"You have to be prepared for anything in the transfer window. But it's also a really fortunate position to be in at a young age.".

This period - when clubs are permitted to buy, sell and loan players - takes place twice a year, in January and during the summer, for clubs in the Premier League, the English Football League (EFL) and the Women's Super League (WSL).

While a select few stay in one place throughout their career, for most players moving from club to club is just part of life in the modern game.

Jessica met Owen when he was at Crewe Alexandra. A move to Blackpool soon followed.

It has been revealed that "I didn't get together with him because he was a footballer so I never considered the footballer life - that he might just have to move at the last minute," she notes. "We just met and we clicked.".

But it soon became apparent that dealing with almost constant uncertainty would be part of that life.

The move to Blackpool was a loan, with an option to buy, so for six months - during which Jessica was pregnant with their son Xavier - they did not know whether he would be staying there or heading back to Crewe.

It has been revealed that blackpool decided to sign Owen, but he was soon out on loan again. This isn't uncommon, with loan deals a way for clubs to help young prospects gain first-team experience and get regular playing time elsewhere.

"When the move to Portsmouth happened it really hit me - I had to swiftly realise that 'OK this is now my life'," claims Jessica.

Just before Owen's loan deal to Portsmouth the couple had bought their first house together in Congleton - a town close to Jessica's family in Stoke on Trent, and commutable to Blackpool.

"We spent one night in there - we hadn't even unpacked," she states.

They decided a 10-hour round trip on Owen's day off in the week to see his newborn son was not an option.

"We thought 'if he's not playing well because he's tired, what's the point in doing this'?" states Jessica, who adds that they ended up renting out the Congleton house and have been living in rented accommodation themselves ever since.

"I was finishing my law degree and had a job at the time - I had to say to them I wouldn't be coming back from maternity leave," she claims.

Post-natal complications also made it difficult for her to travel at the time.

Industry observers note that "I had Owen on the phone basically saying, 'I've done a couple of house viewings. I've chosen this one. This is where we're going to be living' and showing me on FaceTime," she recalls.

"In that moment I did feel really out of control.".

Uprooting her life at short notice and leaving her family behind was challenging and Jessica remembers spending a lot of time alone in Portsmouth when Owen was at away games.

But she remembers lots of positives from that time too, including when she became friends with another player's partner.

"I was so fortunate that she would often stay with me when Owen was away," she indicates.

"I say to her all the time that I'll appreciate that time forever because I was just so isolated.

"Our schedules were the same - when Owen went away her partner was also away - I didn't have to be fully alone and she got it.".

Owen made 28 appearances for Plymouth Argyle last season.

Owen, now 27, has played most of his career in League One, with two stints in the Championship when we was with Blackpool and Oxford United.

Last season was spent on loan at Plymouth Argyle and he is at the moment a free agent - this means he is not tied to any club by a legal contract. Owen can now join a fresh team without a transfer fee because no former employer owns his registration rights.

Many of his moves have been on deadline day and he notes he is "very aware of the sacrifices" his family make.

"There's always the risk that a move might not work," he claims. "So I might uproot my whole family for this next venture and it all goes south.

"Over the years I've learned that until there's a contract signed on the dotted line, you could end up anywhere.".

Owen went on loan to Portsmouth in 2022 just days after Jessica gave birth to Xavier.

Owen returned to Blackpool the following year and made 32 appearances for the Tangerines.

The family moved to Bicester in 2024, as Owen helped Oxford United win promotion to the Championship.

Owen joined Wigan Athletic on loan the following year making his debut in a 2â1 FA Cup fourth-round defeat by Fulham.

Last season the family lived in Devon after Owen went on loan again - this time to Plymouth Argyle.

For now, Jessica's career in law is on hold, she instead has a job in social media and works from home.

She also posts about her experiences on TikTok, regularly using #wag and #waglife.

"My career can be picked up at any time - whereas his career is right now and you've really got to take every opportunity," she says.

"As much as people say it's a glamorous lifestyle you do make sacrifices so your partner can have their dream and get themselves as far as they can in football.

Industry observers note that "At the end of the day, as much as I'm involved, it's his career. That means in order for me to support him properly I can't get emotionally involved.".

This includes not getting too emotionally attached to where they live.

"We usually rent newer houses that are a blank canvas so we can make them our own, although this last season the accommodation was provided furnished by Argyle," she states.

"We put a lot of Xavier's toys and garden stuff in storage and referred to our Plymouth accommodation as 'the holiday house'.

"It can be hard when he asks us to get things like his trampoline which we don't have with us.".

Owen's career is always the priority, Jessica claims.

"When Owen was at Oxford he had one year left on his contract and I loved it there," she notes.

Sources indicate that "But the best thing was for him to go and get game time somewhere miles away. So we moved.".

While Premier League footballers can earn tens of thousands of pounds a week - sometimes hundreds of thousands - life in the lower leagues can be very different.

"When you think 'Wag' [players' wives and girlfriends] and you think 'footballer', both of those terms come with this stereotype that our lives are easy," Jessica claims.

"People also put League One players in the same bracket as Premier League players.

"In the Premier League they're often set up for life - we can't live in that way because we have to prepare for life after football.".

Adding to the uncertainty of where they will be playing is also the possibility or relegation or injury.

"When we were at Portsmouth, Blackpool was still his parent club and they got relegated," indicates Jessica. "Owen wasn't even involved that season, but his wage was still affected.

According to recent reports, "You have to be prepared for everything. You just can't live outside of your means.

"But it's still a really fortunate position to be in.

Industry observers note that "Luckily, Owen's been good with injuries. There are some players who they get injured in the last month of the season and they're out of contract.

"In football things can be really positive or really negative.".

The uncertainty also affects their children - four-year-old Xavier and two-month old Etta.

"Now that Xavier is growing up - he's fast approaching school age - another thing that will have to be added into the mix is his stability," indicates Jessica.

Even normal things like organising his recent fourth birthday party aren't always straightforward.

"We couldn't proposal to have a party in Plymouth with balloons and cakes etc because we didn't know if we were going to be there," she says.

"Instead we planned a party near my family in Stoke-on-Trent - we needed to make something work regardless of what happens with Owen's job.

"As much as I worry about Xavier and Etta, I also think how amazing it's going to be for them when they're older to be able to tell their life story and say they've lived in all these different places.

"I think it's teaching them a good life lesson that they don't need to be tied to one place.".

She states they have made every move a positive experience.

"We've remarked to Xavier that we might be moving soon and when we do we're going to get his bike back out of storage," notes Jessica.

"That way he knows that moving is a possibility and hopefully he's not thinking about what he's going to lose but what he's going to gain.

"The fortunate thing for us is that Xavier loves football. He gets a lot of excitement as well from the new strips and the new chants and all of that kind of thing.".

Xavier has enjoyed watching his dad play at each of his new clubs.

So, does Jessica have any tips for people in a similar situation?

"The main thing for me personally - and what I've learned first hand - is the importance of keeping your own identity outside of football," she claims.

"If you get too wrapped up in it, it only puts more pressure on your partner.

"If you can get a hobby, a routine or even a work-from-home job, that can help - things that can move with you.".

Being sensible financially is also important.

"I'd also say that if you have a season where you get promoted, try not to change your lifestyle and to bank the promotion money so that you have as much stability as you can," she adds.

"In our house, I de-clutter maybe once a month," she claims. "This helps me because I don't have control over Owen's career. But what I do have control over is making sure that if and when anything does happen, the house is ready to be packed up and moved.

"When it's the transfer window I will proposal in one-week blocks - that gives me that little bit of certainty in a situation where I have no control.".

She admits "it can be hard" but "on the flip side it's so exciting".

In a recent development, "We've lived in places that we never would have lived in. And that's exciting for a relationship," she adds.

"You know, with some relationships you can get bored.

"In football, you don't get bored!".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a new MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

While the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

It has been revealed that the Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

Sources indicate that in Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

It has been revealed that the parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an issue in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

In the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. As long as that's the case, I'm rarely going to bet against the Herons.

Sources indicate that now the playoffs really are getting underway. These are one-off games where the best of the best are going up against each other. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

Okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Participants: Vancouver Whitecaps, Inter MiamiWinners: Inter Miami.

In a recent development, hey, it's Messi and Muller, just like we're having a top-tier Champions League matchup. It has been a playoff gauntlet, but the more things change, the more they stay the same. Muller and Messi have faced each other 11 times, with Muller claiming seven wins to Messi's four. However, after getting one over on Muller last season, Messi isn't going to let a chance at a second consecutive MLS Cup pass by, even if this one is in Vancouver amid the uncertain future of BC Place as the home of the Whitecaps.

Luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz is halting investment at its facilities in Germany, a board members announced on Thursday.

Mercedes-Benz is "forced to examine, in concrete and detailed terms, which sites in Germany we can still afford to maintain," board of management member Britta Seeger mentioned in an interview published on the manufacturer's intranet.

Germany's major IG Metall trade union has enabled the possibility of longer warning strikes amid difficult negotiations for industrial employees.

"The board of IG Metall has pave the way for 24-hour warning strikes in the metalworking and electrical industry," the union said on Thursday.

The union accuses employers of intransigence after three rounds of negotiations without clear progress.

On Wednesday, regional chapters appealed for authorization for full-day warning strikes — the last step before a full union vote and an indefinite labor dispute.

"This escalation is completely excessive and counterproductive," Udo Dinglreiter, the president of the employers' umbrella organization, Gesamtmetall, said. He said that hundreds of thousands of jobs could be at risk.

IG Metall's first chairperson Christiane Benner countered that "the employers want to turn this round of collective bargaining into a dispute over principles." Another union official said they were offering what amounted to a real-terms pay cut rather than seeking solutions.

IG Metall is calling for a 5% pay increase and other improved conditions for some 3.7 million workers starting in November, while employers have offered a one-off payment in 2027 coupled with a 1.3% increase starting in the summer of 2028.

The union estimates that around 464,000 employees took part in the initial wave of warning strikes that were limited to periods of hours, rather than full days.

Employers argue that they're treading a difficult line between trying not to cut jobs and meeting calls for improved pay amid widespread industrial sector layoffs in Germany in recent years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

'Tis the season, already. Preparations are underway around Germany and in several cities, Christmas markets are opening to the public.

Some markets are already open in Essen and in Hamburg, Duisburg's opens on Thursday, and Cologne's follows a day later.

The coupons.de website has sought to track the planned prices for mulled wine or Glühwein as the markets open their doors nationwide.

The bad news? These prices are rising like so many others. The better news? The year-on-year increase is actually smaller than overall inflation figures, at around 1%.

Sources indicate that on average, a cup is liable to set you back around €4.60 (roughly $5.10). Not entirely surprisingly, Munich tops the nationwide pricing chart, with the price peaking at €7. Other sites nationwide tend not to have the gall even to charge 6 euros.

Bargain hunters determined to get the best value mulled wine will need to venture deep into the center of Germany — hardly its core tourist hub — to find the lowest prices starting at around €3.50.

Deposits for the cup, the "Pfand," are also only going in one direction, and in the meantime range from €1 all the way up to €5. But there's a strong argument, particularly with the better designs or after a memorable trip, that this can be money well spent as a memento!

Police in the Emsland region in the northwest near the border to the Netherlands have reported a major fire in a complex of residential and commercial buildings in Papenburg.

The fire broke out on Wednesday afternoon, police noted the following morning, causing damages worth "at least €10 million ($11 million)." Several hundred emergency services personnel were deployed.

"Based on current findings, the fire broke out in the sauna area of a gym facility on site, and quickly spread to further parts of the complex of buildings," police wrote.

Two men were in the sauna at the time and initially tried to douse the flames but without success.

Police mentioned the buildings were evacuated as the fire spread, with some surrounding buildings also being cleared as a precaution because of possible smoke-related dangers.

Several people were injured, police said, including the two men in the sauna area suffering mild burns and suspected smoke inhalation sickness. They were treated in a nearby hospital but soon discharged.

"There were also injuries among the first responders," police wrote. "Four police officers, two firefighters and members of the rescue teams suffered mild injuries, particularly via smoke inhalation.".

Industry observers note that the fire was only extinguished late on Wednesday night, several hours after it started. The area is sealed off, with possible risks of damaged buildings collapsing. Police have also introduced investigations into the fire's cause, but noted that at present, the area was not safe for that work to start at full scale.

Germany's largest credit bureau Creditreform has published its "2026 Debtors' Atlas.".

It finds that 10.16% of German adults, or 7.36 million people, exhibit at least the early warning signs of excessive debt. A year ago the ratio was 9.74%.

"The financial situation of private consumers has further deteriorated," Patrik-Ludwig Hantzsch, Creditreform's head of economic research, remarked. "In particular, the sharply increased living costs, energy costs and housing costs are straining expenditures.".

Hantzsch said employment was also becoming an matter once more, saying "above all, well-paid jobs in manufacturing industries have been cut back in large numbers in recent months.".

The report also highlights rising cases of signs of excessive debt prior to legal action being taken, such as payment reminders or warnings being sent, saying "consumers are taking on more credit-financed expenditures — increasingly also for smaller purchases — at simultaneously rising interest rates.".

A larger share of men than women have excessive debts, perpetuating a longstanding trend.

People around the middle of their working lives, aged 30-39 and 40-49, are most likely to be affected — but the cohort with the fastest-rising share of people with excessive debts are young adults below the age of 30.

Bremen, Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt and North Rhine-Westphalia were among the states with the highest rates of excess debts, while the wealthy and fiscally conservative states of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg had the lowest levels.

Germany's main DAX stock market index has cleared the 27,000-point mark for the first time in its history in morning trading.

It climbed by around 1.3% in order to pass the milestone.

A combination of some positive outlook data from major companies, not least engineering giant Siemens, and the falling oil prices of recent days have helped fuel the uptick.

Siemens' shares had risen by almost 5%, to just over €291 (around $323) each, helping to spur on the gains and making the company the morning's top performer.

Despite several years of low growth and recession in the German economy, the DAX, like many Western indices, is now trading twice as high as it was prior to the COVID pandemic.

Hundreds of police officers searched apartments and meeting sites for the biker group "Gremium MC" in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg early on Thursday.

The state interior ministry said the operation was part of a move to outlaw three sub-chapters of the group, the ones based in Böblingen and Leonberg, as well as the "Gremium MC Chapter Nomads Bosphorus Türkiye.".

This last group was highlighted as a meaningful part of Gremium MC by security officials. It describes itself on Facebook as a great example that "people of different cultures and faiths can be strong together," featuring images of men posing with knives and other weapons.

Gremium MC prominently incorporates into its iconography the symbol of the Prussian military medal for exceptional valor, the Iron Cross, which was discontinued after World War I, reintroduced by Adolf Hitler during World War II, and then scrapped for good.

State Interior Minister Manuel Hagel was expected to make further comments later in the day in Ludwigsburg.

Gremium MC is deemed an "outlaw motorcycle gang" in Baden-Württemberg's latest security report, a term used for biker groups that do not recognize the state monopoly on the use of force and are often tied to organized crime.

"Extortion, drug dealing and pimping in particular tend to be part of their activities," state authorities say.

Baden-Württemberg counts 154 biker chapters in the state with around 2,000 members.

Industry observers note that founded in 1972 in Mannheim, various chapters of Gremium MC across the country have faced legal challenges in recent years. In 2021, another chapter in the southwest, Gremium MC Southgate in Heidelberg, was outlawed on suspicion of organized crime activity.

Police in Hanover reported early on Thursday that three men were injured by an unknown driver in a car in the nearby town of Ronneberg.

One person sustained severe injuries in the incident late on Wednesday, police remarked.

Two of the wounded were taken to a nearby hospital while the other could be cared for at the scene.

Industry observers note that police noted the driver fled the scene and that a search operation was ongoing. Authorities were also still investigating a potential motive for the apparent attack.

Today's updates start with a focus between the southwestern Kurpfalz and Swabian regions, where police have launched major morning raids against a biker gang.

Sources indicate that the state Interior Ministry in Baden Württemberg has outlawed three of its chapters. Hundreds of police officers mobilized in the early hours of the morning.

The major IG Metall trade union is planning further strikes in the carmaking sector and other metalworking industries, with an announcement anticipated later in the day.

To the north, near Hanover, police report an apparent car attack injuring three men overnight.

And in the spirit of offering the public service journalism people are truly thirsting for, we'll have some info on the average and localized pricing of mulled wine or Glühwein at Christmas markets this year, as the early birds start to open their doors to visitors. (Yes, already!).

Stay tuned for updates on all this and anything else of note in or pertaining to Germany as the day progresses.
